svg.text: GEOGRAPHICAL DISTRIBUTION OF 8 STUDY TOLL PLAZAS ACROSS INDIAN NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
Empirical Field Study Corridors: NH-44 (North-South), NH-16 (East Coast), NH-65 (Interstate), NH-75 (Peninsular Trunk)

g.text: • In lower-volume passenger corridors (TP02, TP03), K reaches
8.06% to 8.68% due to concentrated daily commuter demand.
• When ADT exceeds 13,000 veh/day and commercial freight rises,
K flattens into a tight asymptote: 6.54% to 6.60%.
Continuous 24-hr freight logistics spreads demand uniformly across all hours.
INSIGHT 2: Freight Amplification of Equivalent PCU
• At TP05 (Chintapally, NH-65), ADT is 13,248 veh/day, but PCU
surges to 24,611 PCU/day (+85.8% expansion above raw volume).
• Driven by 40.73% Heavy Vehicles (MAVs and 3-axle haulers)
possessing Indo-HCM equivalency factors ranging from 2.5 to 4.5.
Demonstrates why physical vehicle count grossly underestimates toll capacity needs.
• Coastal / Interurban (NH-16, NH-75): Higher private car shares,
pronounced seasonal peaks, responsive to peak toll pricing.
• Industrial Freight Spines (NH-44, NH-65, NH-163): High multi-axle
volumes, sustained nocturnal flows, high pavement damage factors.
LOOCV ensures model validation across both distinct regimes without leakage.
